title: It Is Not That…, It Is That…: Correcting an Idea

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *no es que* + subjunctive, *sino que* + indicative from B2 Unit 5. It rejects a reason or an idea someone might assume, and gives the true one: *No es que no quiera, sino que no puedo*. The first part is not stated as a fact, so it takes the subjunctive; the second part is a fact, so it takes the indicative. It suits La Paz and El Alto, two cities people often mix up.

sections.title: Correcting ideas about La Paz and El Alto
rows: No es que El Alto sea un barrio de La Paz, sino que es otra ciudad.
It is not that El Alto is a district of La Paz; it is another city.
No es que el teleférico sea solo para turistas, sino que lo usan muchas personas para ir al trabajo.
It is not that the cable car is only for tourists; many people use it to go to work.
No es que se vistan así solo en las fiestas, sino que muchas llevan pollera todos los días.
It is not that they dress like this only at festivals; many wear the *pollera* every day.
No era que estuvieran lejos, sino que la cuesta hacía largo el viaje.
It was not that they were far apart; the slope made the journey long. (past: imperfect subjunctive, then imperfect)

items.spanish: No es que El Alto sea una ciudad pequeña, sino que ha crecido muy rápido.
items.english: It is not that El Alto is a small city; it has grown very fast.

items.spanish: No es que La Paz sea la capital constitucional, sino que es la sede del gobierno.
items.english: It is not that La Paz is the constitutional capital; it is the seat of government.

items.spanish: No es que los cholets sean solo casas, sino que tienen tiendas y salas.
items.english: It is not that cholets are only houses; they have shops and halls.

sections.content: Use *sino que* before a conjugated verb. If you only change one word, *sino* alone is enough: *No es un barrio, sino una ciudad*. *Pero* would only add a limit; *sino que* replaces the wrong idea.
